Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 82, English)
A Live Aura-Checking Session: How the Guru Fulfills a Devotee's Desir es, the "Concept of the Apple," and the Practice of Gratitude

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn aura-checking (aura-chking) session. Like Sessions 74, 75, and 79, this session is structur ed almost entir ely ar ound live practice — an extended one-by-one r oll call of r egister ed practitioners' auras, checked for negativity , pitru (ancestor) influence, tantra prayog, and siddhi — interspersed with substantial teaching segments and live personal exchanges. Because the primary content is live checking and live back-and-forth rather than conventional narrated doctrine, Part I her e documents the session's format, its r ecurring teaching themes, and illustrative (anonymized, wher e individual r eadings ar e involved) patterns rather than pr esenting a number ed doctrinal sequence. Per Ashaeiynn's own stated policy against publicly exposing individuals' specific negativity/pitru/tantra diagnoses in a sensationalized way , this document generalizes and anonymizes personal r eadings rather than r epr oducing every attendee's specific r esult.
1. Session Opening and Exam Banter

Per this teaching's live texture, the session opens casually , with sangat members greeting each other and Bhaiya asking a student how his exam went, followed by light banter about whether Hanuman ji Maharaj might have "helped" with the exam if only the student had prayed beforehand.
2. Teaching: How the Guru Fulfills a Devotee's Desir es

Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains that Baba (his own guru) never interferes in ordinary tasks or competitions on a devotee's behalf — no matter how someone performs, no external power intervenes unless the outcome would also serve someone else's genuine benefit and the guru chooses to help. However , once someone becomes truly dear to their guru, the guru quietly maintains a running account of everything that person's heart desires (a partner , a family , wealth, comfort, respect) and steadily fulfills it — often precisely because the devotee never explicitly asked.
3. Bhaiya's Personal Story: The Eighteen-Month Test of Faith

Per this teaching, Bhaiya shares an extended personal account: early in his own sadhna, his guru told him to perform hawan continuously for no stated purpose. For about a year and a half he obeyed without explanation, even as money went out and nothing visibly changed. His family — including his own younger brother — began to openly call him mentally unwell, suggested he see a doctor , and turned against him; he describes crying quietly most nights, continuing his three remaining activities (crying, sitting, and japa), and privately doubting himself even while continuing to ask his guru, in meditation, "Am I doing something wrong?" His guru's only reply was always the same: "Keep doing what I have told you to do." Per this teaching, this period caused significant emotional trauma, and only years of hindsight allowed him to recognize the eighteen months as a period of accelerated growth compressed into a short span.
4. Teaching: The Indirect Fulfillment of Desir es

Per this teaching, Bhaiya illustrates with an example: neighbors once asked him to pray that they get a petrol pump business; he asked his guru, who instructed hawan; the petrol pump itself never came, but everything the petrol pump was meant to provide (fortune, stability) came anyway — because what a person actually wants beneath a stated wish (e.g., "water") is usually a deeper underlying need (e.g., "peace"), and it is that underlying need the guru fulfills, not necessarily the literal request.
5. Opening Prayer and Sankalp for Register ed Practitioners

Per this teaching's live practice, a formal prayer is of fered on behalf of "Ashaeiynn ke Parikshit Bhaiya," invoking Hanuman ji Maharaj's grace over the sankalp (resolve), japa, and tapasya of all registered attendees, so that each may be counted among the guru's accepted disciples.
6. The Aura-Checking Format

Per this teaching's live practice, the session's core activity is a long roll call: attendees are named one at a time (by full name, sometimes muted/unmuted to confirm they are present and japa-ing), and Bhaiya reports, for each, whether negativity , pitru (ancestor) influence, tantra prayog, or siddhi is present — often with a brief remedy or encouragement.
7. Common Categories of Findings

Per this teaching's live practice, across the many individual checks in this session, findings generally fell into a small number of recurring categories: no negativity or pitru issue at all (the most common result, often accompanied by a comment on a practitioner's visible siddhi or a devata's grace); a pitru (ancestral) influence, ranging from mild ("a couple of ancestors quietly waiting nearby") to disruptive (ancestors deliberately creating obstacles because a family's traditional occupation or unfinished ritual obligation has been abandoned); a tantra prayog (an external ritual working directed at the person, described as distinct from both negativity and pitru influence); and, occasionally , a lingering non-family entity (such as an external shakti "seated" in a household through past worship) requiring a specific remedy .
8. Common Remedies Pr escribed

Per this teaching's live practice, the remedies given repeatedly across individual checks include: lighting 1 1 diyas (lamps) daily without fail, especially for those unable to maintain regular japa; a "tel vidhi" (oil-of fering practice) for negativity; a "jal vidhi" (water practice) for household or entity-related disturbances; a "gol vidhi" (a specific multi-day ritual, e.g., three sittings of eleven days) for certain tantra-related bodily symptoms; attending the upcoming Purnima hawan; and, for household-level disturbances, simply continuing consistent practice rather than provoking or confronting the disturbance directly .
9. Teaching: Defending the Guru Against Critics

Per this teaching, in response to the recurring experience of outsiders dismissing Ashaeiynn or claiming its practices rely on "ghosts" rather than genuine divine power , Bhaiya of fers a test: before believing criticism, ask two questions — is Parikshit Bhaiya greater than Hanuman ji Maharaj, and is Ashaeiynn greater than Hanuman ji Maharaj? Since the answer is clearly no, and since all activity here proceeds only under Hanuman ji's sanction, no valid basis exists for dismissing the practice; anyone is free to test this claim by directing the same skepticism at their own tradition, since no one can prove whose practice channels which kind of power .
10. Teaching: Ashaeiynn as a Place Where Every Kind of Power Gathers

Per this teaching, because Hanuman ji Maharaj is described as sovereign over every realm — commanding the respect of every power , benevolent and malevolent alike — a fortress under his protection will naturally attract every kind of ener gy , from the most sattvic to the most negatively af flicted, since the same pull that draws positive ener gy also draws negative ener gy seeking release; this is of fered as the explanation for why both healing and heavy negativity are visibly present within the community .
1 1. A Live Exchange: Requesting Advanced Sadhna Permission

Per this teaching's live practice, one practitioner asked permission to perform japa at all hours since she could not attend night sessions; Bhaiya explained that continuous, round-the-clock japa requires first completing a deeper practice ("gehan tatva") and receiving the guru's explicit permission through a mentor , obtained through sustained prayer rather than simply requested outright.
12. Teaching: Why Ancestors (Pitru) Sometimes Obstruct Devotees

Per this teaching, in several individual cases, Bhaiya explained that a family's ancestors are not opposed to a descendant's current work in principle, but object specifically when a descendant abandons the family's traditional occupation; per this teaching, a person facing chronic, unexplained obstruction in a business unrelated to their family's historic trade was advised to learn what that traditional occupation was and reconnect with it, since ancestral support flows more readily toward continuity than toward departure.
13. Teaching: Ancestors Also Cause Friction to Pr event Spiritual Pr ogr ess

Per this teaching, Bhaiya explains that some pitru deliberately create friction or distraction (heaviness in the shoulders, mental agitation, demotivation) specifically to prevent a descendant's japa from progressing too far , since increased spiritual power in the family line would create a kind of tension ("gharshan," friction/burning sensation) for unsettled ancestors; consistent prayer and dedicated diyas for the pitru are the recommended remedy in these cases.
14. Extended Teaching: The "Concept of the Apple"

Per this teaching, Bhaiya revisits an earlier -taught metaphor: an apple sealed in an isolated box will not disappear but will gradually decompose, changing form again and again over time while never losing its underlying ener gy — it merely takes on dif ferent appearances. Per this teaching, spirits (bhoot-pret) operate the same way: what looks like a lingering negative entity today is, over time, the same ener gy changing form, and a being that appears troubling now may — after enough devotional transformation — become a source of real help and power later; declaring something "not a real spirit" or "just superstition" at any single point in that process, per this teaching, misunderstands that all beings (including devatas) pass through lower states before reaching higher ones.
15. A Live Illustration: A Family Ancestor's Gradual Transformation

Per this teaching, Bhaiya of fers a specific illustration (kept general here per Ashaeiynn's privacy practice around individual family details): a practitioner's ancestor , initially experienced as an obstructive presence, was gradually transformed through roughly eighteen months of the practitioner's sustained devotion — its ener gy softening and changing character over that period — illustrating the "apple" teaching in practice: the same underlying entity , given devoted attention, changes its expression over time rather than needing to be forcibly expelled.
16. Teaching: Suffering Recognized by Reputable Figur es Is Not Automatically Illegitimate

Per this teaching, Bhaiya references a well-known contemporary spiritual figure whose practice some critics dismiss as relying on lower spirits ("karan pishachini"), and ar gues that regardless of how one categorizes the method, its results (guiding lar ge numbers of people toward faith) speak for themselves — contrasted with those who merely pretend to sit in meditation with a deity without producing any comparable outcome.
17. A Live Testimony: Fifteen Years of Negativity Resolved

Per this teaching's live practice, one practitioner shared, with visible emotion, that a negativity she had lived with for roughly fifteen years was reported clear in this session's check — describing it as a major turning point not just for herself but for her whole family , after having previously spent significant money on negativity-removal elsewhere without success; she credited a specific hawan recommended by her mentor , completed less than a month earlier , along with her own prior prayer that she be found free of negativity by the time of this aura check.
18. A Live Anecdote: An Astral Encounter During Diya-Daan

Per this teaching's live practice, one practitioner described waking during the night after an eleventh-day diya of fering to see a faceless, limbless, black-colored figure near his feet; Bhaiya explained this as a benign ener gy summoned by the practitioner's own subtle body during his practice (one of several such companion ener gies present, not alone), present specifically because he was undistracted and deeply focused at that hour — clarifying that "negative" specifically means something that insults or actively harms a person, which this was not.
19. A Live Dr eam Account: The Guru Saving Disciple and Guide fr om a Cliff

Per this teaching's live practice, one practitioner described a dream/meditative vision in which "Parikshit Bhaiya" pushed him of f a cliff into a ravine, after which the practitioner's guru (Baba) rescued both of them and brought them safely back up; Bhaiya interpreted this as a strongly positive sign of surrender — being "pushed" symbolizing complete submission at the guru's feet, with the guru's rescue affirming that total submission is always met with protection.
20. Teaching: Humility and Staying at the First Stage of Sadhna

Per this teaching, Bhaiya reflects that practitioners who advance to higher stages of sadhna (second, third, fourth, fifth stage, up to samadhi) often develop subtle ego from their greater power , since arrogance eventually diminishes any person who carries it; Bhaiya states that he personally prefers to remain "stuck" at the first stage rather than risk the ego that can accompany higher attainment, framing this as wanting to remain his own guru's smallest, humblest devotee rather than pursuing status.
21. Teaching: Wealth, Burden, and True Riches

Per this teaching, Bhaiya observes that many extremely wealthy people (citing high-value Delhi/Gur gaon properties with unused pools and gyms) are trapped servicing the debt behind their own success and have no time to enjoy what they've acquired, and that a person for whom the divine steadily provides — even modestly — is truly the wealthiest, since loneliness and ego commonly accompany those who reach the highest visible peaks.
22. Closing Devotional Singing

Per this teaching's live practice, the individual aura-checking segment concludes with an extended devotional singing session — a medley including Ram bhajans ("Mere Ram," praising Ram's qualities and relationship to Hanuman) and a Hanuman Chalisa-style composition ("Dukhit Dayal Birudu Sambhari").
23. Teaching: Gratitude (Shukrana) as a Spiritual Practice

Per this teaching, following the singing, Bhaiya teaches that daily gratitude toward God is a distinct and essential practice, separate from asking for things; he specifically references the Islamic practice of five daily prayers and the concept of shukrana (thanks), noting that the specific power of gratitude is visibly concentrated in sites associated with sustained collective gratitude practice (citing MeccaMedina as an example), and states that a person who learns to say thank you daily will always keep moving forward.
24. Teaching: Not Judging Others' Spiritual Methods

Per this teaching, extending the earlier "apple" teaching, Bhaiya cautions against the reflexive habit of labeling any spiritual practice one doesn't recognize as illegitimate ("that's ghosts, not devatas") — ar guing there is no objective way to prove whose practice channels divine power and whose does not, and that every powerful entity , including every devata, was once "lesser" before growing into its current stature.
25. Closing Logistics: Announcing a New Series and a Time Change

Per this teaching's live practice, the session closes with Bhaiya announcing that the community's next session will begin a new teaching series, and that going forward the group will meet at 8:30 rather than the previously later start time, to give both the sangat and Bhaiya
more rest between sessions.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

A guru does not interfere in ordinary competitive tasks (like exams), but a devotee's deeper , often unstated heart's desires are steadily and quietly fulfilled over time as they grow close to their guru — often via the underlying need behind a wish rather than the literal request itself. Bhaiya's own eighteen-month period of unexplained hawan practice — during which his family doubted his sanity — is of fered as a model of sustained obedience to a guru's instruction despite the absence of visible results or explanation. This session's core activity was a live, one-by-one aura check of registered practitioners for negativity , pitru (ancestral) influence, tantra prayog, and siddhi, with common remedies including 1 1 daily diyas, tel vidhi, jal vidhi, gol vidhi, and attending the Purnima hawan. Pitru (ancestors) may obstruct a descendant's unrelated ventures when a family's traditional occupation has been abandoned, or may create friction/distraction specifically to slow a descendant's spiritual progress; consistent prayer and dedicated diyas are the standard remedy in both cases. The "concept of the apple" teaches that spiritual ener gies (including seemingly negative ones) never lose their underlying power — they simply change form over time, meaning a currently troubling presence may , through sustained devotion, transform into a source of real help. Per Ashaeiynn's own privacy practice, this document does not exhaustively list individual practitioners' specific negativity , pitru, or tantra diagnoses from this session. Daily gratitude (shukrana) is taught as a distinct, essential spiritual practice in its own right, separate from petitionary prayer , and is described as a major source of sustained spiritual power . Practitioners are cautioned against reflexively dismissing unfamiliar spiritual practices as illegitimate, since no one can prove whose tradition channels genuine divine power and whose does not — and every powerful being was once lesser before it grew . Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .

Bot Response Guidelines

Do not reproduce or invent any specific individual practitioner's negativity , pitru, or tantra diagnosis from this session — per Ashaeiynn's own stated privacy practice, such details are intentionally generalized/anonymized in this knowledge base. Present Bhaiya's personal eighteen-month testing story (Q3–Q4) with appropriate emotional weight — it is of fered as a model of sustained obedience under uncertainty , not as encouragement to ignore genuine medical or family concerns. Present the "concept of the apple" (Q14–Q15) and the caution against judging other traditions (Q23) as this teaching's own specific framing, not as a demand that all spiritual claims be treated as equally valid.
